newsitem.title: INDONESIA: Election-related violence kills 14 in East Timor.
newsitem.headline: Election-related violence kills 14 in East Timor.

text.p: At least 14 people died in a wave of election violence in East Timor, including a soldier killed by rebels on Thursday while guarding a polling booth as millions of Indonesians voted in general elections.
Analysts said the violence, including attacks on polling booths over a wide area, appeared to be acts of defiance by opponents of Indonesia's rule in the former Portuguese colony.
East Timor police chief Colonel Yusuf Muharam, speaking by telephone from the East Timor capital Dili, said the soldier was shot and killed near Hatolia in Ermera district.
"He was guarding the ballot box. He was shot by rebels," Muharam said, adding that he was the only victim in the incident.
Local sources said nine soldiers had died in the clash, but there was no immediate confirmation.
Residents reported other attempts overnight to destroy polling stations in Ermera, about 45 km (28 miles) southwest of Dili, and other districts east and west of Dili.
"The Indonesian government has always said that voter turnout is a good indicator of support for integration but this time someone has decided to act against this," one diplomat said.
However, police and residents said voting was generally peaceful through the day in East Timor.
The military estimates there are about 80 anti-Indonesian guerrillas operating in the rugged territory, although other sources say there could be as many as 200.
The Indonesian armed forces maintain a strong presence in East Timor.
Muharam said police shot dead four rebels in an attack on a mobile brigade or riot police post on the outskirts of Dili on Wednesday night.
He said rebels had also shot and killed nine civilians in two other incidents.
"From the rebels there were four dead and four captured alive. They received gunshot wounds. Four police were injured by gunfire. No police were killed," Muharam said.
"They were trying to seize weapons from the guard post, but they failed," he said.
"In Baucau, there were two citizens shot dead. In Los Palos, there were seven citizens shot dead and two seriously injured," Muharam said.
Diplomatic analysts said it was the biggest surge in deadly violence in East Timor in recent years.
Indonesia invaded East Timor in 1975 and annexed the territory the following year as its 27th province in a move still not recognised by the United Nations.

Portuguese Foreign Minister Jaime Gama, speaking in Sintra, Portugal, condemned Indonesia's handling of the elections in the territory and said Lisbon had made a formal complaint to the United Nations and also made contacts with its European Union partners.
One diplomat who watches East Timor closely said the territory had been very tense since two police were killed in an ambush on Tuesday by a platoon-sized unit of rebels near Baucau.
A similiar sized rebel unit was involved in an ambush in Viqueque last month in which four soldiers and two government officials were killed.
